intro.title: Margin Collapse
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple webpage with stacked paragraphs to visually explore how margin collapse works in CSS. You will learn the core concept that when vertical margins of adjacent elements touch, they combine into a single margin instead of adding together. The main technologies involved are CSS margin properties and the box model. By adjusting margins on different elements, you'll see how this behavior affects spacing and layout. This foundational knowledge will help you predict and control spacing in your web designs more effectively.
intro.usecase: Margin collapse is a crucial CSS concept that developers encounter daily when building consistent spacing in real-world interfaces. You'll see it in action when creating navigation menus where list items need consistent vertical spacing, in dashboard cards that stack neatly without excessive gaps, or in article layouts where paragraphs and headings should have predictable spacing. Understanding margin collapse helps you avoid unexpected spacing issues in forms, modals, and content panels, ensuring your UI elements align perfectly without manual adjustments.
